title.zh: 卷317 列傳一百四 王无党 吴进义 谭行义 李勋 樊廷 武进升 马负书 范毓皛
title.en: Volume 317 Biographies 104: Wang Wudang, Wu Jinyi, Tan Xingyi, Li Xun, Fan Ting, Wu Jinsheng, Ma Fushu, Fan Yuxiao
title.raw: 卷317 列傳一百四 王无党 吴进义 谭行义 李勋 樊廷 武进升 马负书 范毓皛

sentences.zh: 范毓皛}}

translations.literal: Fan Yuxiao}}
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuxiao

sentences.zh: =王無黨=王無黨，直隸萬全人。

translations.literal: Wang Wudang — Wang Wudang, a native of Wanquan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wudang was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年武進士，授藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he became a military jinshi and was appointed a Blue Finch plume guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: He took his military jinshi degree in the fifty-first year of the Kangxi reign and was appointed a Blue Finch plume guardsman.

sentences.zh: 累遷廣西梧州協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to brigade deputy commander at Wuzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to brigade deputy commander at Wuzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 貴州台拱九股苗為亂，無黨率師討定之，擢左江鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the Nine-stock Miao of Taigong in Guizhou rebelled, Wudang led troops to suppress and settle them, and was promoted to regional commander of the Zuojiang garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine-stock Miao of Taigong in Guizhou rose in revolt, Wudang led an expedition that pacified them and was promoted to regional commander of the Zuojiang garrison.

sentences.zh: 九股苗復為亂，無黨馳抵古州，分兵赴八寨督剿。

translations.literal: When the Nine-stock Miao rebelled again, Wudang hurried to Guzhou, divided his forces, and went to Bazhai to supervise the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine-stock Miao rebelled again, he rushed to Guzhou, detached columns, and personally supervised operations at Bazhai.

sentences.zh: 經略張廣泗檄無黨分攻台拱大台雄，克之。

translations.literal: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi ordered Wudang to attack separately at Taigong, Daitai, and Xiong, and they were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi directed Wudang to assault Taigong, Daitai, and Xiong in separate columns, and all were captured.

sentences.zh: 平交上等三十餘寨，擒其渠巴利，會收牛皮大箐。

translations.literal: He pacified more than thirty stockades including Jiaoshang, captured their leader Bali, and together recovered Niupi Daqing.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified more than thirty stockades including Jiaoshang, seized their chieftain Bali, and jointly cleared Niupi Daqing.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，署貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he acted as provincial military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign he served as acting provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 從廣泗撫定上下九股諸苗從為亂者。

translations.literal: Following Guangsi, he pacified the upper and lower Nine-stock Miao who had joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Guangsi he pacified the upper and lower Nine-stock Miao who had taken part in the revolt.

sentences.zh: 二年，真除。

translations.literal: In the second year he received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year his appointment was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 疏陳黔省急務，請籌積貯，築城垣，整墩台塘房，禁掠賣人口，下部議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized on urgent affairs in Guizhou, asking to build up stores, erect city walls, put beacon towers, posts, and guardhouses in order, and forbid the abduction and sale of people; the ministries deliberated and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on Guizhou's pressing needs, urging grain reserves, city fortification, repair of beacon towers and guard posts, and a ban on kidnapping people for sale; the ministries approved and implemented the measures.

sentences.zh: 定番州屬姑盧寨苗視險強肆，廣泗與無黨遣漢、土官兵三千餘，分道毀寨搜箐，擒其渠老排，十餘日而定，上褒其妥協。

translations.literal: Miao of Guluzhai subordinate to Dingfan prefecture relied on rugged terrain and acted violently; Guangsi and Wudang sent more than three thousand Han and native troops, destroyed stockades and searched ravines by separate routes, captured their leader Laopai, and settled matters in little more than ten days; the throne praised their well-judged handling.
translations.idiomatic: Miao of Guluzhai under Dingfan relied on difficult ground and raided boldly; Zhang Guangsi and Wudang sent over three thousand Han and native troops along separate routes to raze stockades and comb the ravines, seized their chieftain Laopai, and restored order within a fortnight; the emperor commended their measured conduct.

sentences.zh: 四年，陛見，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he had audience at court and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was received in audience and awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 六年，移湖廣提督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 黑峒苗為亂，大學士鄂爾泰以無黨在貴州久，熟苗事，留使戡定乃上官。

translations.literal: The Heidong Miao rebelled; Grand Secretary Ortai, because Wudang had long been in Guizhou and knew Miao affairs well, kept him to suppress the trouble before he took up his new post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heidong Miao rebelled, Grand Secretary Ortai—knowing Wudang's long service in Guizhou and his familiarity with Miao affairs—detained him to finish the campaign before he assumed the Huguang post.

sentences.zh: 八年，上以湖廣軍政廢弛，無黨至官未有所整理，下詔詰責。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because Huguang military administration was lax and Wudang had done nothing to set it in order since taking office, an edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor, finding Huguang military administration neglected and Wudang still without reforms after taking office, issued an edict of reprimand.

sentences.zh: 十三年，坐提標兵救火攘衣物，兵部論無黨徇庇，當奪官，命詣京師引見，左授湖南沅州協副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because troops of his command banner plundered clothing while fighting a fire, the Board of War judged Wudang guilty of shielding them and deserving dismissal; he was ordered to the capital for audience and demoted to brigade deputy commander at Yuanzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his banner troops were found looting goods while fighting a fire; the Board of War held that Wudang had covered for them and should be stripped of rank. Summoned to the capital for audience, he was demoted to brigade deputy commander at Yuanzhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 遷雲南楚姚鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of the Chuyao garrison in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of the Chuyao garrison in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 內擢鑾儀使。

translations.literal: He was promoted within the capital to Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in the capital to Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 复外授福建漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Again he was sent outside the capital as regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was again posted outside the capital as regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以目疾乞罷。

translations.literal: Because of eye disease he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement on account of eye trouble.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡壯愨。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: =吳進義=吳進義，字子恆，陝西寧朔人。

translations.literal: Wu Jinyi — Wu Jinyi, style name Ziheng, a native of Ningshuo in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jinyi, whose style name was Ziheng, was a native of Ningshuo in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父開圻，康熙二十七年一甲三名武進士，官至雲南元江副將。

translations.literal: His father Kaiqi was a third-place military jinshi of the first class in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi and rose to vice commander at Yuanjiang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kaiqi had placed third among military jinshi of the first class in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi and rose to vice commander at Yuanjiang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 進義入伍，從振武將軍孫思克徵噶爾丹，劄署守備，發江南借補千總。

translations.literal: Jinyi entered the ranks, followed General Sun Sike of Zhenwu in the campaign against Galdan, was provisionally appointed garrison commander, and was sent to Jiangnan to fill a company captain's post on loan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyi enlisted and followed General Sun Sike of Zhenwu against Galdan, served provisionally as garrison commander, and was lent to Jiangnan to fill a company captaincy.

sentences.zh: 累遷江南壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to regional commander of the Shouchun garrison in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to regional commander of the Shouchun garrison in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 擢江南提督，疏言：「太湖界江、浙，漁船姦良難辨。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan and memorialized: "Taihu lies on the border of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and on fishing boats the honest and the wicked are hard to tell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan, he memorialized: "Taihu straddles the Jiangsu–Zhejiang border, and on fishing boats honest folk and criminals are hard to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 請照海洋例巡哨，支河小汛，飭兩省陸路兵巡查，則聲勢聯絡，姦宄斂跡。」

translations.literal: I ask that patrols follow the maritime precedent; at branch rivers and minor flood seasons, order land forces of both provinces to inspect, so that our strength is linked and evildoers will shrink away."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that patrols follow the maritime precedent; on branch streams and at minor flood seasons, order land troops of both provinces to inspect jointly, so our forces act in concert and wrongdoers will keep out of sight."

sentences.zh: 有旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 久之，移浙江，再移福建，復還浙江。

translations.literal: After a long while he was moved to Zhejiang, then again to Fujian, and returned once more to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was transferred to Zhejiang, then to Fujian, and later back to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時有偽為孫嘉淦疏稿語訐上，進義與浙閩總督喀爾吉善以聞。

translations.literal: At the time a forged memorial in Sun Jiagan’s name used language that impeached the throne; Jinyi and Zhejiang–Fujian Governor-General Ka'erjishan reported it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a forged memorial bearing Sun Jiagan's name contained language attacking the throne; Jinyi and Zhejiang–Fujian Governor-General Ka'erjishan reported it together.

sentences.zh: 上令究所從來，語連提督廨胥吏，喀爾吉善劾進義隱諱，命解官聽讞。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered investigation of its origin; the affair implicated clerks of the commander's yamen; Ka'erjishan impeached Jinyi for concealment, and he was ordered dismissed pending trial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the source traced; the inquiry touched clerks in the commander's yamen. Ka'erjishan impeached Jinyi for concealment, and he was dismissed pending trial.

sentences.zh: 進義力辨未嘗隱諱，其幕客證進義已見稿。

translations.literal: Jinyi vigorously argued he had never concealed anything; his staff testified that Jinyi had already seen the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyi insisted he had never concealed anything; members of his staff testified that he had already seen the draft.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫雅爾哈善論進義當重闢，上愍其老，命貰罪。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Ya'erhashan argued Jinyi deserved execution; the emperor pitied his age and ordered punishment commuted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Ya'erhashan argued that Jinyi deserved execution; the emperor, taking pity on his age, commuted the penalty.

sentences.zh: 復以疏稿未得作偽主名，令江蘇巡撫莊有恭會鞫。

translations.literal: Because the forger of the memorial had not been identified, Jiangsu Governor Zhuang Yougong was ordered to join in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Because the forger had still not been identified, Jiangsu Governor Zhuang Yougong was ordered to join the investigation.

sentences.zh: 有恭疏陳進義實未見稿，浙江承審諸吏牽合附會。

translations.literal: Yougong memorialized that Jinyi had in fact not seen the draft and that the Zhejiang examining clerks had forced the case together.
translations.idiomatic: Yougong memorialized that Jinyi had never seen the draft and that the Zhejiang examining officials had stitched the case together by conjecture.

sentences.zh: 事下軍機大臣覆訊，得實。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to Grand Council ministers for re-examination and proved true.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to Grand Council ministers for re-examination and was found to be true.

sentences.zh: 上以進義無辜廢斥，召來京，命以提督銜署直隸宣化鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Jinyi had been dismissed without guilt, summoned him to the capital and ordered him to serve as acting regional commander of the Xuanhua garrison in Zhili with the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Jinyi innocent yet wrongly dismissed, the emperor summoned him to the capital and appointed him acting regional commander of the Xuanhua garrison in Zhili with provincial-commander rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授古北口提督。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed provincial military commander of Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed provincial military commander of Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 進義請限操演火藥，增設河屯協弓兵，皆允行。

translations.literal: Jinyi asked that drill with gunpowder be regulated and that bow troops be added to the river garrison brigade; all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyi requested limits on live-fire drill and additional bow troops for the river garrison brigade; both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒，年八十四，加太子太保，諡壯愨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died at eighty-four; he was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died at eighty-four; he was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and titled Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 進義家世多武功，從祖坤，貴州永北總兵，嘗徵四川苗及金川有功。

translations.literal: Jinyi's family for generations produced military merit; his collateral ancestor Kun was regional commander of Yongbei in Guizhou and had merit campaigning against Sichuan Miao and in Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyi's family had long produced distinguished soldiers; his collateral ancestor Kun, regional commander of Yongbei in Guizhou, had earned merit against Sichuan Miao and in the Jinchuan campaigns.

sentences.zh: 坤子開增，自武舉官至浙江溫州總兵。

translations.literal: Kun's son Kaizeng rose from military licentiate to regional commander of Wenzhou in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's son Kaizeng rose from military licentiate to regional commander of Wenzhou in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: =譚行義=譚行義，四川三台人。

translations.literal: Tan Xingyi — Tan Xingyi, a native of Santai in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xingyi was a native of Santai in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，以武舉授陝西西寧衛千總。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period, as a military licentiate he was appointed company captain of the Xining guard in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, as a military licentiate he was appointed company captain of the Xining guard in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，從軍平青海，再遷河南城守營參將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he followed the army to pacify Qinghai and was again promoted to colonel of the Henan garrison battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he campaigned in Qinghai and was promoted to colonel of the Henan garrison battalion.

sentences.zh: 河東總督田文鏡劾行義送陝西軍馬疲瘦，奪官，上令來京引見，召對稱旨，賜編刻上諭、貂皮、香珠，復原官。

translations.literal: Hedong Governor-General Tian Wenjing impeached Xingyi for delivering Shaanxi army horses worn and thin; his office was taken, but the emperor ordered him to the capital for audience; his responses pleased the throne, and he was given engraved imperial pronouncements, sable fur, and fragrant pearls, and his post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong Governor-General Tian Wenjing impeached him for delivering worn and emaciated Shaanxi army horses; he was dismissed, but the emperor summoned him to the capital. His answers in audience pleased the throne, and he received engraved imperial pronouncements, sable fur, and fragrant pearls; his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 再遷廣東高雷廉總兵。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to regional commander of Gaolei and Lian in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to regional commander of the Gaolei and Lian garrisons in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 總督鄂彌達檄行義將五千人協剿貴州亂苗，進擊滾縱、高表諸寨。

translations.literal: Governor-General E'ermida ordered Xingyi to lead five thousand men in joint suppression of rebellious Miao in Guizhou and advance against the stockades of Gunzong, Gaobiao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General E'ermida ordered Xingyi to lead five thousand men against rebellious Miao in Guizhou and to assault the stockades of Gunzong, Gaobiao, and others.

sentences.zh: 經略張廣泗令赴援上江，攻烏婆、擺吊諸險要地，搜牛皮大箐，獲其魁。

translations.literal: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi ordered him to reinforce the upper river, attack the strategic places of Wupo and Baidiao, search Niupi Daqing, and capture their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Guangsi sent him to reinforce the upper river, storm the strongpoints of Wupo and Baidiao, comb Niupi Daqing, and capture the rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 歷福建漳州、湖南鎮筸諸鎮。

translations.literal: He served in turn at the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian and the Zhenbian garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as commander at Zhangzhou in Fujian and at Zhenbian in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年，授廣西提督，帥師會討楚、粵亂苗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong he was appointed provincial military commander of Guangxi and led troops in joint operations against rebellious Miao in Huguang and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianlong he was appointed provincial military commander of Guangxi and led troops in joint campaigns against rebellious Miao in Huguang and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 宜山縣土蠻恃險劫掠，行義與總督馬爾泰、署巡撫安圖令游擊楊剛討之。

translations.literal: Native tribesmen of Yishan county relied on rugged terrain to plunder; Xingyi, together with Governor Ma'ertai and acting Governor Antu, ordered Colonel Yang Gang to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Native tribesmen in Yishan relied on difficult terrain to raid; Xingyi, with Governor Ma'ertai and acting Governor Antu, ordered Colonel Yang Gang to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 破白土、丘索二村，執其渠，斬以徇。

translations.literal: He broke the two villages of Baitu and Qiusuo, seized their leader, and executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He overran the villages of Baitu and Qiusuo, seized their leader, and executed him as an example.

sentences.zh: 忻城土縣外八堡有劇盜曰藍明星，恃險焚劫。

translations.literal: Outside the eight forts of Xincheng native district there was a notorious bandit named Lan Mingxing who relied on rugged terrain to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the eight forts of Xincheng native district a notorious bandit named Lan Mingxing used the rugged country to burn and plunder.

sentences.zh: 行義檄副將畢映捕治，明星遁入山，搜捕得之。

translations.literal: Xingyi ordered Brigade Commander Bi Ying to capture him; Mingxing fled into the mountains but was found in the search and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyi ordered Brigade Commander Bi Ying to hunt him down; Mingxing fled into the hills but was found and captured.

sentences.zh: 有黃順者，匿湖北、廣東錯壤處，謀為亂。

translations.literal: There was a Huang Shun who hid in the interlaced borderlands of Hubei and Guangdong and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Huang Shun hid in the interlaced borderlands of Hubei and Guangdong and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 貴州人黎阿蘭與相應，散旗印，將起事。

translations.literal: Li Alan of Guizhou responded to him, distributed banners and seals, and was about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Alan of Guizhou joined him, distributed banners and seals, and was on the verge of revolt.

sentences.zh: 行義诇知之，督兵攻克賊巢，擒斬首從七十餘，事乃定。

translations.literal: Xingyi learned of it through intelligence, led troops to storm the rebel nest, captured and beheaded more than seventy leaders and followers, and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyi learned of the plot through intelligence, stormed the rebel stronghold, and killed or captured more than seventy leaders and followers, after which order was restored.

sentences.zh: 柳州兵皆居草舍，患火。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Liuzhou all lived in thatched huts and suffered from fire.
translations.idiomatic: The troops at Liuzhou all lived in thatched huts and were plagued by fire.

sentences.zh: 行義請發白金四千貸兵建瓦屋，分三年還帑，從之。

translations.literal: Xingyi asked that four thousand taels of silver be issued on loan for the troops to build tile-roofed houses, repaid to the treasury over three years; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyi asked that four thousand taels of silver be lent to the troops to build tiled houses, to be repaid to the treasury over three years; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又有李彩者，糾眾聚遷江石版村謀犯縣城，行義既捕治，請城北設汛。

translations.literal: There was also a Li Cai who gathered a crowd at Shiban village on the Qian River to attack the county seat; after Xingyi had captured and punished him, he asked that a garrison post be set north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Another man, Li Cai, mustered a band at Shiban village on the Qian River to assault the county seat; after Xingyi had captured him, he requested a garrison north of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 尋以擅發倉穀貸於兵，左授登州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for issuing grain from the granary on his own authority to lend to the troops, he was demoted to regional commander of the Dengzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for issuing granary grain on his own authority as loans to the troops, he was demoted to regional commander of the Dengzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷江南提督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，移浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was moved to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，再移福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was again moved to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was again transferred to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，諡恭愨。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died and was given the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he died and was posthumously titled Gongmin.

sentences.zh: =李勳=李勳，貴州鎮遠人。

translations.literal: Li Xun — Li Xun, a native of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was a native of Zhenyuan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 入伍，稍遷守備。

translations.literal: He entered the ranks and was gradually promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted and rose gradually to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從征台拱九股生苗，廣泗檄同剿羊吊、洞裡、羊色諸地，搜牛皮大箐，勳亦在行間。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the raw Miao of the Nine-stock at Taigong; Guangsi ordered joint suppression at Yangdiao, Dongli, Yangse, and other places and a search of Niupi Daqing; Xun was also in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the raw Nine-stock Miao at Taigong; Zhang Guangsi ordered joint operations at Yangdiao, Dongli, Yangse, and elsewhere and a sweep of Niupi Daqing; Xun served in the field throughout.

sentences.zh: 累遷湖廣提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to provincial military commander of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to provincial military commander of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 緬甸亂，移雲南提督。

translations.literal: When Burma was in turmoil he was transferred to provincial military commander of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Burma fell into disorder he was transferred to provincial military commander of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 疏請自普洱馳往孟艮捕治亂渠召散，上以其老，不勝瘴癘，命還普洱。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to hurry from Pu'er to Menggen to capture the rebel leader Zhaosan; the emperor, considering him old and unable to endure miasma, ordered him back to Pu'er.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to ride from Pu'er to Menggen to seize the rebel leader Zhaosan; the emperor, judging him too old to endure the miasmic south, ordered him to remain at Pu'er.

sentences.zh: 勳已至孟艮，督總兵劉德成、華封等葺堡寨，防要隘，得召散兄猛養等。

translations.literal: Xun had already reached Menggen and supervised regional commanders Liu Decheng, Hua Feng, and others in repairing forts and stockades and guarding strategic passes; he captured Zhaosan's elder brother Mengyang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had already reached Menggen and directed regional commanders Liu Decheng and Hua Feng to repair forts, hold the passes, and capture Zhaosan's elder brother Mengyang and others.

sentences.zh: 勳還，卒於途。

translations.literal: On his return Xun died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，諡莊毅。

translations.literal: He was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and titled Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: =樊廷=樊廷，陝西武威人。

translations.literal: Fan Ting — Fan Ting, a native of Wuwei in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ting was a native of Wuwei in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初入伍，更姓名王剛。

translations.literal: When he first entered the ranks he changed his name to Wang Gang.
translations.idiomatic: When he first enlisted he changed his name to Wang Gang.

sentences.zh: 從征烏蒙、青海、西藏，積功累遷甘肅肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns in Wumeng, Qinghai, and Tibet, and through accumulated merit was promoted to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Wumeng, Qinghai, and Tibet and, through accumulated merit, rose to regional commander of the Suzhou garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 自陳復姓名，改籍四川潼川縣。

translations.literal: He petitioned to restore his original name and changed his registration to Tongchuan county in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to resume his original name and transferred his household register to Tongchuan county in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾犯科舍圖卡倫，盜駝馬，其眾二萬餘。

translations.literal: The Dzungars attacked the Keshetu post station, stole camels and horses, and numbered more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Dzungars raided the Keshetu post station and drove off camels and horses; their force exceeded twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 廷率副將冶大雄等將二千人御之，轉戰七晝夜，與總兵張元佐等軍合，殺賊無算，盡還所盜。

translations.literal: Ting led Brigade Commander Ye Daxiong and others with two thousand men to resist them, fought day and night for seven days, joined with the forces of Regional Commander Zhang Yuanzuo and others, killed countless enemies, and recovered all that had been stolen.
translations.idiomatic: Ting led Brigade Commander Ye Daxiong and two thousand men against them, fought seven days and nights, joined Zhang Yuanzuo's force, killed the enemy in great numbers, and recovered everything that had been taken.

sentences.zh: 時提督紀成斌護寧遠大將軍印，聞上，詔褒廷以寡敵眾，忠勇冠軍，賜白金萬，一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: At the time Provincial Commander Ji Chengbin was guarding the seal of the Ningyuan grand general; when the report reached the throne, an edict praised Ting for facing many with few, his loyalty and courage foremost in the army, granted ten thousand taels of silver, and made him hereditary Commandant of Light Chariots of the First Class.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commander Ji Chengbin then held the seal of the Ningyuan grand general; when word reached court, an edict praised Ting for fighting many with few, called his loyalty and courage unmatched in the army, granted ten thousand taels of silver, and ennobled him as hereditary Commandant of Light Chariots of the First Class.

sentences.zh: 授陝西固原提督、都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Guyuan in Shaanxi and Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed provincial military commander of Guyuan in Shaanxi and Vice Commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入覲，請從軍，命從署寧遠大將軍查郎阿出師屯南山。

translations.literal: On entering audience he asked to join the campaign and was ordered to follow Acting Ningyuan Grand General Zhalang'a in taking the field and encamping at Nanshan.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he asked to take the field and was ordered to follow Acting Ningyuan Grand General Zhalang'a, who marched out and encamped at Nanshan.

sentences.zh: 副將軍張廣泗偵賊伏烏爾圖水，檄廷將千五百人自鹼泉子進剿，至哈洮遇賊，奪據山梁，連敗之。

translations.literal: Deputy Grand General Zhang Guangsi detected the enemy lying in wait at the Wueritu River and ordered Ting to lead fifteen hundred men from Jianquanzi in a punitive advance; at Hatao they met the enemy, seized the mountain ridge, and defeated them repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Grand General Zhang Guangsi learned that the enemy lay in ambush at the Wueritu River and ordered Ting forward with fifteen hundred men from Jianquanzi; at Hatao they met the foe, seized the ridge, and routed them again and again.

sentences.zh: 越噶順抵鄂隆吉大坂，殺賊四百，擒三十六，收其糧械。

translations.literal: Crossing Gashun they reached Elongji Daban, killed four hundred enemies, captured thirty-six, and seized their grain and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Gashun they reached Elongji Pass, killed four hundred of the enemy, captured thirty-six, and took their grain and arms.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，上從查郎阿請，發甘、涼諸鎮兵五千人駐哈密，置總統提督，以授廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong, following Zhalang'a's request, the emperor sent five thousand troops from the garrisons of Gansu and Liangzhou to garrison Hami, established a commanding provincial post, and gave it to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign, acceding to Zhalang'a's request, the emperor sent five thousand troops from the Gansu and Liangzhou garrisons to Hami, created a supreme commander's post, and gave it to Ting.

sentences.zh: 廷至軍，疏言：「烏爾克為極西第一要隘，兵出偵洮賴大坂北蘆草溝、噶順溝東亂山子及烏爾圖水，夜輒有火光。

translations.literal: When Ting reached the army he memorialized: "Wuerke is the foremost strategic pass of the far west; troops sent out to reconnoiter toward Taolai Daban saw fires by night north at Lucao Gully, east at Gashun Gully at Luanshanzi, and at the Wueritu River.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the army Ting memorialized: "Wuerke is the foremost pass of the far west; patrols toward Taolai Daban report fires by night north at Lucao Gully, east at Luanshanzi above Gashun Gully, and along the Wueritu River.

sentences.zh: 守隘兵寡，請量增。」

translations.literal: The garrison at the pass is few; I ask that it be increased as needed."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison is too thin; I ask that it be strengthened as needed."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「哈密兵在山南煙墩溝諸地牧駝馬，請分山北防兵巡護。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Hami troops pasture camels and horses south of the mountains at Yandun Gully and other places; I ask that part of the northern defense force be assigned to patrol and protect them."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Hami troops pasture camels and horses south of the mountains at Yandun Gully and elsewhere; I ask that part of the northern garrison be detailed to patrol and protect them."

sentences.zh: 皆用其議。

translations.literal: All his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: All his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 在邊二年，以病乞罷，命還固原治疾，遣醫往診。

translations.literal: After two years on the frontier he asked to retire because of illness; he was ordered back to Guyuan to treat his ailment and a physician was sent to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: After two years on the frontier he asked to retire on account of illness; he was ordered back to Guyuan to recover, and a physician was sent to attend him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於哈密。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Hami.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Hami.

sentences.zh: 遺疏論防邊事甚切，上深愍之。

translations.literal: His final memorial on frontier defense was very earnest, and the emperor was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial on frontier defense was urgent and thorough, and the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 命查郎阿經紀其喪，歸葬涼州。

translations.literal: Zhalang'a was ordered to manage his funeral and return the body for burial at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhalang'a was ordered to arrange his funeral and return the body for burial at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 贈都督同知，諡勇毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Commissioner-in-chief and given the posthumous title Yongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Commissioner-in-chief and titled Yongyi.

sentences.zh: 子經文，官至廣東右翼總兵。

translations.literal: His son Jingwen rose to regional commander of the Guangdong Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingwen rose to regional commander of the Guangdong Right Wing.

sentences.zh: 經文子繼祖，官湖北副將。

translations.literal: Jingwen's son Jizu served as brigade commander in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen's son Jizu served as brigade commander in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 繼祖子從典，請改籍湖北恩施。

translations.literal: Jizu's son Congdian asked to change his registration to Enshi in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu's son Congdian petitioned to transfer his household register to Enshi in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 從典子燮，官湖南永州鎮總兵，同治中，坐事罷。

translations.literal: Congdian's son Xie was regional commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan; in the Tongzhi period he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Congdian's son Xie served as regional commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan; during the Tongzhi reign he was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: =武進升=武進升，山西寧鄉人，其後改籍江南江寧。

translations.literal: Wu Jinsheng — Wu Jinsheng, a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi, later changed his registration to Jiangning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jinsheng was a native of Ningxiang in Shanxi and later transferred his household register to Jiangning in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 初以張姓入伍。

translations.literal: At first he entered the ranks under the surname Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He first enlisted under the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 稍遷浙江溫州鎮標守備。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to garrison commander of the Wenzhou garrison standard in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，閩浙總督滿保疏薦，引見，授三等侍衛，屬怡親王允祥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao memorialized recommending him; after audience he was appointed a third-rank guardsman and attached to Prince Yi Yinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign, Fujian–Zhejiang Governor-General Manbao recommended him by memorial; after audience he was made a third-rank guardsman and assigned to Prince Yi Yinxiang.

sentences.zh: 尋外授江寧游擊。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted outside the capital as colonel at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.

sentences.zh: 言：「閩省不習騎射，加意督率，弓力漸增。

translations.literal: He reported: "Fujian troops are unaccustomed to mounted archery; with special attention to training and command, bow strength has gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Fujian troops were unskilled in mounted archery, but under close supervision bow strength has steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 馬兵出馬收馬較前改觀。」

translations.literal: Cavalry turnout and return of horses show marked improvement over before."
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry turnout and the return of mounts are markedly better than before."

sentences.zh: 高宗諭以「如此方不負任使，然亦不可欲速，尤貴為之以實，要之以久」。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor instructed him: "Only thus do you not fail your commission; yet you must not seek speed—what matters most is doing the work in earnest and sustaining it over time."
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor replied: "That is how you fulfill your charge—but do not hurry. What matters is solid effort sustained over the long term."

sentences.zh: 進升與總督喀爾吉善忤，疏言：「喀爾吉善外似和平，心實剛愎。

translations.literal: Jinsheng clashed with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan appears mild outwardly but is in fact stubborn and self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng fell out with Governor-General Ka'erjishan and memorialized: "Ka'erjishan seems mild in manner but is in fact stubborn and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 令臣密察水師提督張天駿營伍，臣辭以水師非所轄。

translations.literal: He ordered me secretly to inspect the camps of Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun, but I declined on the ground that the navy is outside my jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered me to inspect Naval Commander Zhang Tianjun's camps in secret, but I declined because the navy is outside my jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 督臣正言厲色，必令臣密察。

translations.literal: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I conduct the secret inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The governor spoke sternly and insisted that I carry out the secret inspection.

sentences.zh: 及察知水師陋規，告之督臣，督臣置不問，反與天駿契合。

translations.literal: When I found corrupt practices in the navy and reported them to the governor, he ignored them and instead became intimate with Tianjun.
translations.idiomatic: When I uncovered corrupt practices in the navy and reported them, the governor ignored them and instead grew close to Tianjun.

sentences.zh: 臣察漳州營馬值，總兵馬負書為督臣舊部，巧為徇私。

translations.literal: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu, an old subordinate of the governor, artfully showed favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: When I inspected horse prices in the Zhangzhou garrison, Regional Commander Ma Fushu—an old subordinate of the governor—cleverly bent the rules in his favor.

sentences.zh: 令臣無地自容。」

translations.literal: This left me with no place to hide my shame."
translations.idiomatic: I was left utterly humiliated.

sentences.zh: 又疏言喀爾吉善衰憊狀，上斥進升支離狂率。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's enfeebled condition; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for incoherent and reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on Ka'erjishan's declining health; the emperor rebuked Jinsheng for rambling and reckless accusations.

sentences.zh: 喀爾吉善亦劾進升徇所屬，縱兵行竊。

translations.literal: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for indulging his subordinates and allowing troops to steal.
translations.idiomatic: Ka'erjishan also impeached Jinsheng for favoring his men and allowing troops to plunder.

sentences.zh: 因左授江南狼山鎮總兵，進升疏謝，諭曰：「汝無他過，祗好勝多事，故左授示薄懲。

translations.literal: He was therefore demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; Jinsheng memorialized thanks, and was instructed: "You have no other fault—only love of rivalry and meddling—so the demotion is a light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to regional commander of the Langshan garrison in Jiangnan; in his memorial of thanks he was told: "You have no other fault except competitiveness and meddling; the demotion is meant as a mild warning.

sentences.zh: 若不知改，或遂委靡，一切姑息，皆不可也。」

translations.literal: If you do not reform, or instead become slack and indulge everything, neither is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail to reform, or sink into slack indulgence, either course is unacceptable."

sentences.zh: 居數月，擢江南提督，以老罷。

translations.literal: After several months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; later he retired because of age.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was promoted to provincial military commander of Jiangnan; he later retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 再起，終浙江提督。

translations.literal: Recalled to service, he ended as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Called back to service, he ended his career as provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘，諡良毅。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty and was given the posthumous title Liangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties and was posthumously titled Liangyi.

sentences.zh: =馬負書=馬負書，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Ma Fushu — Ma Fushu, a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fushu was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年一甲一名武進士，授頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was top military jinshi of the first class and was appointed a first-rank guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he placed first among military jinshi of the first class and was appointed a first-rank guardsman.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to regional commander of the Zhangzhou garrison in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「漳州民好鬥，有所謂'闖棍'，結黨肆行，土豪養為牙爪，請嚴治之。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The people of Zhangzhou are fond of fighting; there are so-called 'street brawlers' who band together and act violently, and local bullies keep them as enforcers—I ask that they be sternly suppressed."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The people of Zhangzhou are quarrelsome; gangs of so-called 'street brawlers' roam at will, and local bullies keep them as muscle—I ask that they be sternly suppressed."

sentences.zh: 上下其章喀爾吉善，令體察懲治。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to Ka'erjishan with orders to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Ka'erjishan with orders to investigate and punish accordingly.

sentences.zh: 歷瓊州、金門、台灣、狼山諸鎮。

translations.literal: He served in turn at the Qiongzhou, Jinmen, Taiwan, and Langshan garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn at Qiongzhou, Jinmen, Taiwan, and Langshan.

sentences.zh: 署古北口提督，疏言：「兵習陣法，無濟實用。

translations.literal: As acting provincial military commander of Gubeikou he memorialized: "Troops drill in formations that do not help in real combat.
translations.idiomatic: As acting provincial military commander of Gubeikou he memorialized: "Troops drill in formations that do little in real combat.

sentences.zh: 應於秋冬收穫後，擇地成列，為仰攻旁擊勢。

translations.literal: After the autumn harvest they should choose ground, form ranks, and practice uphill assault and flanking attacks.
translations.idiomatic: After the autumn harvest they should choose ground, form ranks, and practice uphill assaults and flanking attacks.

sentences.zh: 分合進退，以金鼓為節。

translations.literal: Advancing, withdrawing, dividing, and reuniting should follow the beat of gongs and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, withdrawing, dividing, and reuniting should be timed to gongs and drums.

sentences.zh: 常月教場演習，仍依營製。」

translations.literal: Regular monthly drill on the training ground should still follow camp regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Regular monthly drills on the training ground should still follow camp regulations."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved and carried out the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and ordered implementation.

sentences.zh: 授福建陸路提督。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed provincial military commander of Fujian land forces.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡昭毅。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: =范毓皛=范毓皛，山西介休人。

translations.literal: Fan Yuxiao — Fan Yuxiao, a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuxiao was a native of Jiexiu in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 范氏故巨富。

translations.literal: The Fan clan was formerly immensely wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan clan had long been immensely wealthy.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，師徵準噶爾，輸米餽軍，率以百二十金致一石。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period, when the army campaigned against the Dzungars, they supplied grain to feed the troops, generally at a cost of one hundred and twenty taels per picul.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, when armies campaigned against the Dzungars, the family supplied grain to the troops, generally at a cost of one hundred and twenty taels of silver per picul.

sentences.zh: 六十年，再出師，毓皛兄毓馪請以家財轉餉，受運值視官運三之一。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, when the army marched out again, Yuxiao's elder brother Yushen asked to transport provisions with family wealth and received transport fees at one-third of official rates.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, when troops marched out again, Yuxiao's elder brother Yushen offered family wealth to transport provisions and was paid carriage fees at one-third of the official rate.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，師出西北二路，怡親王允祥薦毓馪主餉，計穀多寡，程道路遠近，以次受值，凡石米自十一兩五錢至二十五兩有差，累年運米百餘萬石。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, when armies took the two northwest routes, Prince Yi Yinxiang recommended Yushen to manage provisions; grain amounts and distances were calculated and fees taken in order—from eleven taels five mace to twenty-five taels per picul—and over successive years more than a million piculs of grain were transported.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongzheng reign, when armies marched by the two northwest routes, Prince Yi Yinxiang recommended Yushen to manage supplies; fees were set by grain volume and distance, ranging from eleven taels five mace to twenty-five taels per picul, and over the years he transported more than a million piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 世宗特賜太僕寺卿銜，章服同二品。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor specially granted him the rank of Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with insignia and dress equal to the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor specially granted him the rank of Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with insignia and dress of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 寇犯北路，失米十三萬餘石，毓馪斥私財補運，凡白金百四十四萬。

translations.literal: When the enemy invaded the northern route and more than one hundred thirty thousand piculs of grain were lost, Yushen spent private wealth to make up the transport, altogether one million four hundred forty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck the northern route and more than one hundred thirty thousand piculs of grain were lost, Yushen spent private funds to make up the shipments, totaling one million four hundred forty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 師既罷，米轉運近地，戶部按近值核銷，故所受遠值，責毓馪追繳，凡白金二百六十二萬，復出私財採蓡，市銅供鑄錢以償。

translations.literal: After the campaign ended, grain was transported to nearby places and the Board of Revenue audited payment at nearby rates; therefore the higher fees received for distant transport were charged back to Yushen for recovery—two million six hundred twenty thousand taels of silver in all—and he again spent private wealth gathering ginseng and buying copper to supply coinage for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign ended, grain was moved to nearby depots and the Board of Revenue settled accounts at local rates; Yushen was therefore ordered to repay the difference on distant hauls—two million six hundred twenty thousand taels in all—and again spent private funds gathering ginseng and buying copper for minting to meet the debt.

sentences.zh: 毓皛以武舉授衛千總，以駝佐軍，擢守備。

translations.literal: Yuxiao, as a military licentiate, was appointed company captain of a guard; he assisted the army with camels and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao entered service as a military licentiate appointed company captain of a guard; he supplied camels to the army and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷直隸天津鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several posts to regional commander of the Tianjin garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to regional commander of the Tianjin garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 自河南河北鎮移廣東潮州，疏請令潮州營兵如河北例，兼習長槍、短棍、連接棍諸藝。

translations.literal: Transferred from the Henan–Hebei garrison to Chaozhou in Guangdong, he memorialized asking that Chaozhou garrison troops, following the Hebei precedent, also train in long spear, short staff, and linked staff.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred from the Henan–Hebei garrison to Chaozhou in Guangdong, he memorialized asking that Chaozhou troops, following the Hebei precedent, also drill in long spear, short staff, and linked staff.

sentences.zh: 世宗命與總督鄂彌達、提督張溥商榷。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor ordered consultation with Governor-General E'ermida and Provincial Commander Zhang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered him to consult Governor-General E'ermida and Provincial Commander Zhang Pu.

sentences.zh: 鄂彌達等上言：「廣東山海交錯，軍械惟鳥槍最宜，次則弓箭、藤牌、挑刀、大砲。

translations.literal: E'ermida and others reported: "Guangdong's mountains and sea interweave; among arms the musket is most suitable, next bows and arrows, rattan shields, pole blades, and cannon.
translations.idiomatic: E'ermida and others reported: "Guangdong's terrain mixes mountain and sea; muskets suit it best, followed by bows, rattan shields, pole blades, and cannon.

sentences.zh: 毓皛所議與廣東不甚宜。」

translations.literal: What Yuxiao proposed is not very suitable for Guangdong."
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao's proposal is not well suited to Guangdong."

sentences.zh: 上韙鄂彌達等議，仍諭毓皛初至，當嘉其肯言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved E'ermida's view but still instructed that since Yuxiao had just arrived, his willingness to speak should be commended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with E'ermida but still told Yuxiao that, as a newcomer, his willingness to speak out deserved praise.

sentences.zh: 嘉應、潮陽遇颶，海岸決。

translations.literal: Jiaying and Chaoyang were struck by typhoons and the coast broke.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaying and Chaoyang were struck by typhoons and the sea walls gave way.

sentences.zh: 毓皛以聞，命加意撫綏。

translations.literal: Yuxiao reported it and was ordered to give special care to relief and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao reported the disaster and was ordered to give special attention to relief and pacification.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，署廣東提督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he acted as provincial military commander of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign he served as acting provincial military commander of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 故事，市舶至，詣海關納稅。

translations.literal: By precedent, when trading ships arrived they went to the customs house to pay tax.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, trading ships paid duties at the customs house on arrival.

sentences.zh: 或遇風未至所往地，中道暫泊，亦論稅如例。

translations.literal: If wind held them from their destination and they anchored midway, tax was still assessed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: If storms kept them from their destination and they anchored en route, duties were still assessed as usual.

sentences.zh: 毓皛慮民避屢稅，遇風不敢泊，致傾覆，疏請商舟寄泊，非即地市易不徵稅，上命待審察。

translations.literal: Yuxiao feared that people would avoid repeated taxation and, meeting wind, dare not anchor and so capsize; he memorialized asking that merchant vessels be allowed to anchor temporarily without tax unless they traded on the spot, and the emperor ordered the matter held for review.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao feared merchants would avoid repeated duties, refuse to anchor in storms, and capsize; he memorialized that temporary anchorage should be tax-free unless goods were sold on the spot, and the emperor ordered the proposal held for review.

sentences.zh: 毓皛以憂歸，服終，授直隸正定鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Yuxiao returned home for mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed regional commander of the Zhengding garrison in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao returned home to mourn; after the mourning period he was appointed regional commander of the Zhengding garrison in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督阿爾賽請移任苗疆，上不允，諭以「毓皛富家子弟，謹慎無過。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor-General A'ersai asked that he be transferred to the Miao frontier; the emperor did not agree and instructed: "Yuxiao is the son of a wealthy family, cautious and without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Governor-General A'ersai asked that he be transferred to the Miao frontier; the emperor refused, saying: "Yuxiao is a wealthy man's son—careful and without fault.

sentences.zh: 苗疆事重，不能勝也」。

translations.literal: Miao frontier affairs are weighty; he cannot bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: Miao frontier affairs are too weighty for him to bear."

sentences.zh: 上巡五台，毓皛言兄毓馪子清注具羊千、馬十備賞賚，上卻之。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured Wutai, Yuxiao said that his brother Yushen's son Qingzhu had prepared a thousand sheep and ten horses as gifts for bestowal; the emperor declined them.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's tour of Wutai, Yuxiao reported that his brother Yushen's son Qingzhu had prepared a thousand sheep and ten horses as gifts; the emperor declined them.

sentences.zh: 尋以老罷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he retired because of age.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：提鎮雖專閫，然受制於督撫，所轄兵散處諸營汛，都試肄武，虛存其制耳。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Although provincial commanders and regional commanders hold independent authority, they are constrained by governors-general and governors; the troops under them are scattered among garrison posts, and the triennial capital military examinations and training exist only as empty forms.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Although provincial and regional commanders held independent commands, they remained subordinate to governors-general and governors; their troops were scattered across garrison posts, and the triennial capital examinations and drill existed largely as empty forms.

sentences.zh: 無黨、進義皆能勤其官者，行義捕盜，廷屢從戰，皆有勞。

translations.literal: Wudang and Jinyi were both diligent in office; Xingyi captured bandits; Ting repeatedly followed campaigns—all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wudang and Jinyi were diligent in office; Xingyi suppressed bandits; Ting fought in many campaigns—all earned merit.

sentences.zh: 進升龂龂不欲曠其職。

translations.literal: Jinsheng was contentious and unwilling to neglect his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsheng was exacting and unwilling to neglect his duties.

sentences.zh: 毓皛與其兄出私財助軍興，幾傾其家而不悔，求諸往史，所未有也。

translations.literal: Yuxiao and his brother spent private wealth to aid military campaigns, nearly ruining the family without regret—a thing sought in past histories but never found.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiao and his brother spent private wealth to support the armies, nearly ruining their house without regret—a devotion unmatched in the histories.
